answer.summary: Scrum can help teams break work into smaller increments, get customer feedback sooner, and improve their collaboration through retrospectives. Perri emphasizes agile principles over rigidly following every process step, but the evidence does not specify when a team can dispense with a formal framework altogether.

sections.heading: Practices that help a team benefit from Scrum
sections.content: Chunk work down and seek customer feedback faster rather than spending years building without showing the product to anyone. The Scrum master’s role is to help the team work well together and improve how it does Scrum; retrospectives at the end of a sprint let the team discuss what went well and what did not, then inspect and adapt its process.

sections.heading: Principles over rigid process
sections.content: Perri says the goal of agile is to move quickly and deliver customer value. Teams benefit from embracing those principles; treating agile as a cut-and-dry process that requires every step to be followed is not useful if it loses sight of why the work is being done. The evidence does not give a specific condition under which a team would not need a formal framework.
